fatal_errors: The proposed intervention changes elemental ratios outside the specified equiatomic quinary, quaternary, and ternary alloy set.

It replaces the target temperature-dependent mechanisms—MSAD-controlled glide resistance, cryogenic inertial dulling, and high-temperature solute pinning—with an SFE-centered room-temperature mechanism.
It conflates reduced SFE-driven suppression of dynamic recovery and increased work hardening with solid-solution strengthening and yield strength.
The room-temperature-only design cannot detect the cryogenic or Portevin–Le Chatelier regimes central to the target.
explanation: The hypothesis is scientifically plausible as an alternative study of non-equiatomic Co/Cr-rich alloys, and E2 directly supports the claimed direction of SFE, lattice-friction, and work-hardening changes. However, it does not reconstruct the controlled comparison among equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni subsets or the single-crystal CRSS-versus-temperature investigation. It omits strain-rate jumps, thermal-activation fitting, MSAD calculations, cryogenic phonon-drag effects, and high-temperature serrated flow. Its TEM and mechanical measurements are testable, but composition simultaneously changes SFE, modulus, lattice friction, phase stability, and possible ordering, so correlation would not uniquely establish SFE causality. The falsification rule is also too weak because requiring no significant change in SFE, strength, or work hardening allows the mechanism to survive when strength changes without SFE. E1 supports thermally activated solid-solution hardening rather than the proposed SFE mechanism, while E2 describes an already established design concept, limiting novelty.
